newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-STICH THROUGH TO GERMAN OPEN SECOND-ROUND.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-STICH THROUGH TO GERMAN OPEN SECOND-ROUND.

text.p: Former Wimbledon champion Michael Stich, who said last week he would retire at the end of the year, cheered up his local fans on Monday with a win over Slovakia's Karol Kucera in the first round of the German Open.
The 28-year-old German's assured 6-4 6-4 victory over Kucera was the highlight of a day on which rain caused play to be called off in the early evening.

"Of course I went out to win. If that wasn't the case I would have stopped yesterday, not in four months. Until then my goal is to continue to play well in tournaments," said Stich who is quitting tennis because of a recurring shoulder injury.
Spaniard Sergi Bruguera also went through to the second-round with a 6-0 6-4 win over Australia's Scott Draper.

Rain was not the only disappointment on the first day of the $2.3 million tournament. American Andre Agassi angered German officials by announcing he was withdrawing just a day before he was due on court because of a recurrent wrist injury.
Spaniard Carlos Costa replaces Agassi and meets German Daniel Elsner in the first-round.
